'''''Lavandula pinnata''''' (also known as '''fernleaf lavender''' and '''jagged lavender''')<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Haddou |first1=Mounir |last2=Elbouzidi |first2=Amine |last3=Taibi |first3=Mohamed |last4=Baraich |first4=Abdellah |last5=Loukili |first5=El Hassania |last6=Bellaouchi |first6=Reda |last7=Saalaoui |first7=Ennouaamane |last8=Asehraou |first8=Abdeslam |last9=Salamatullah |first9=Ahmad Mohammad |last10=Bourhia |first10=Mohammed |last11=Nafidi |first11=Hiba-Allah |last12=Addi |first12=Mohamed |last13=Guerrouj |first13=Bouchra El |last14=Chaabane |first14=Khalid |date=2024-04-08 |title=Exploring the multifaceted bioactivities of Lavandula pinnata L. essential oil: promising pharmacological activities |journal=Frontiers in Chemistry |language=English |volume=12 |doi=10.3389/fchem.2024.1383731 |doi-access=free |pmid=38660570 |pmc=11041020 |bibcode=2024FrCh...1283731H |issn=2296-2646}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Lavandula pinnata {{!}} fern leaf lavender Shrubs/RHS Gardening |url=http://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/61298/lavandula-pinnata/details |access-date=2024-06-20 |website=www.rhs.org.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the mint family, [[Lamiaceae]], native to southern [[Madeira]] and the [[Canary Islands]] (Lanzarote). It was first described in 1780.<ref name=WCSP_109066/>

==Description==
''Lavandula pinnata'' is a [[shrub]] growing between 18 and 24 inches in height, with opposite, simple, pinnately dissected [[leaf|leaves]], and square stems. Leaves are covered in fine white hairs, giving the plant a downy appearance. Flowers are deep violet in colour,<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 20, 2024 |title=Growing Lavandula pinnata |url=https://www.gardenia.net/plant/lavandula-pinnata |website=Gardenia.net}}</ref> with single or triple flower spikes, blooming from late spring to summer.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Haddou |first1=Mounir |last2=Elbouzidi |first2=Amine |last3=Taibi |first3=Mohamed |last4=Baraich |first4=Abdellah |last5=Loukili |first5=El Hassania |last6=Bellaouchi |first6=Reda |last7=Saalaoui |first7=Ennouaamane |last8=Asehraou |first8=Abdeslam |last9=Salamatullah |first9=Ahmad Mohammad |last10=Bourhia |first10=Mohammed |last11=Nafidi |first11=Hiba-Allah |last12=Addi |first12=Mohamed |last13=Guerrouj |first13=Bouchra El |last14=Chaabane |first14=Khalid |date=2024-04-08 |title=Exploring the multifaceted bioactivities of Lavandula pinnata L. essential oil: promising pharmacological activities |journal=Frontiers in Chemistry |language=English |volume=12 |doi=10.3389/fchem.2024.1383731 |doi-access=free |pmid=38660570 |pmc=11041020 |bibcode=2024FrCh...1283731H |issn=2296-2646}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
{{As of|2018|February|4}}, the original authorship of the name "''Lavandula pinnata''" varies by source. The [[World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]] attributes the name to [[Johan Daniel Lundmark]] in 1780,<ref name=WCSP_109066/> a view followed by [[The Plant List]] and [[Tropicos]]. [[Germplasm Resources Information Network|GRIN Taxonomy]] and the African Plant Database attribute the name to [[Carl Linnaeus the Younger|the younger Carl Linnaeus]] (1780); the [[International Plant Names Index]] has the same attribution, but without a date, as well as noting the use of the name by [[Conrad Moench]] in 1802.
